name: Atmospheric neutrino mixing measurement with IceCube DeepCore

significance.note: Not a significance-based claim; the paper reports parameter constraints.
significance.quote: we constrain the atmospheric neutrino mixing parameters to be $\sin^2\theta_{23} = 0.51\pm 0.05$ and $\Delta m^2_{32} = 2.41\pm0.07\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{eV}^2$, assuming a normal mass ordering.

summary.plain: IceCube's DeepCore sub-array measured how atmospheric neutrinos change type on their way through the Earth, using 2011–2019 data with improved calibration. The collaboration says the 40% error reduction makes this the most precise measurement of oscillation parameters using atmospheric neutrinos, and that the results are compatible and complementary to those from accelerator beams.
summary.technical: Three-flavour atmospheric oscillation fit to 2011–2019 DeepCore data with improved calibration and processing: sin²θ₂₃ = 0.51 ± 0.05 and Δm²₃₂ = (2.41 ± 0.07) × 10⁻³ eV² for normal ordering, a 40% error reduction over the previous IceCube result.

title: Measurement of Atmospheric Neutrino Mixing with Improved IceCube DeepCore Calibration and Data Processing
why_it_matters: The abstract says the results are compatible and complementary to those obtained using accelerator neutrino beams, which are measured at lower neutrino energies and are subject to different sources of uncertainties.
